svg.text: The three push buttons: BUILD, ACTION, MENU
Zoom on the UPPER breadboard. Each button: leg 1 → free hole in its ESP32 pin column (rows f-i), leg 2 → upper − rail.
Buttons sit on the cardboard. One M-F wire per leg: female end on the button leg, male end in the breadboard. 2 wires per button.
ESP32 (top row of pins in row j)
MENU: leg 1 → D14 column (5th pin from the left), row g. leg 2 → upper − rail
BUILD: leg 1 → D26 column (7th pin from the left), row h. leg 2 → upper − rail
ACTION: leg 1 → D25 column (8th pin from the left), row i. leg 2 → upper − rail
Any free green hole (rows f, g, h, i) in the right column works. The rows above are just to keep the wires apart.
Upper − rail must reach GND: M-M from the ESP32 GND column (2nd pin) to the rail, or a − to − link from the lower board.
4-leg buttons: use two legs on DIAGONALLY opposite corners, so they are always on different sides of the switch.
